```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Workflow: validate settings -> read and audit saved rows -> summarize ratios/tests
# -> build g2 -> export figures, tables, and reproducibility records.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
  fig.width = 12, fig.height = 9, out.width = "100%", fig.align = "center", dpi = 160)
needed <- c("ggplot2", "patchwork")
missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Install these packages before knitting: ",
  paste(missing, collapse = ", "), ". For example: install.packages(c('ggplot2', 'patchwork')).")
if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") < "3.4.0") stop("ggplot2 >= 3.4.0 is required.")
library(ggplot2)
# Knitting supplies params from YAML. These defaults also permit Run All / Run
# Above in an interactive R session, so the plot object g2 remains in that session.
default_params <- list(
  results_dir = ".",
  file_pattern = "^seed[0-9]+[.][Rr][Dd][Aa][Tt][Aa]$",
  output_dir = "variance_type1_conditionalX2_gexp_plots",
  scenarios = c("i", "ii", "iii"), n_min = 300, n_max = 2100,
  alpha = 0.05, null_value = 0, mc_conf_level = 0.95, band_alpha = 0.18,
  invalid_policy = "report", check_scenario2_settings = TRUE,
  variance_y_min = 0.7, variance_y_max = 1.2, type1_y_max = 0.115,
  save_pdf = TRUE, save_plot_object = TRUE
)
if (!exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) params <- default_params
# Do not replace explicitly supplied NULL values: these select automatic axes.
for (nm in setdiff(names(default_params), names(params))) params[nm] <- default_params[nm]
options(width = 100)
#' Validate a probability-valued report setting
#'
#' Check that an input is one finite numeric probability strictly between zero and one.
#'
#' @param x Value to check.
#' @return Scalar logical TRUE if all checks pass, FALSE otherwise.
is_prob <- function(x) is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1L && is.finite(x) && x > 0 && x < 1
#' Validate a finite numeric scalar setting
#'
#' Check numeric type, scalar length, and finiteness.
#'
#' @param x Value to check.
#' @return Scalar logical TRUE for one finite numeric value, FALSE otherwise.
is_scalar <- function(x) is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1L && is.finite(x)
stopifnot(is_prob(params$alpha), is_prob(params$mc_conf_level),
  is_scalar(params$null_value), is_scalar(params$band_alpha),
  params$band_alpha > 0, params$band_alpha <= 1,
  is_scalar(params$n_min), is_scalar(params$n_max), params$n_min >= 1,
  params$n_max >= params$n_min, params$invalid_policy %in% c("report", "stop"),
  is.logical(params$save_pdf), length(params$save_pdf) == 1L, !is.na(params$save_pdf),
  is.logical(params$save_plot_object), length(params$save_plot_object) == 1L,
  !is.na(params$save_plot_object))
scenario_levels <- c("i", "ii", "iii")
selected_scenarios <- scenario_levels[scenario_levels %in% unlist(params$scenarios)]
if (!length(selected_scenarios) || any(!unlist(params$scenarios) %in% scenario_levels))
  stop("params$scenarios must contain one or more of 'i', 'ii', 'iii'.")
if (xor(is.null(params$variance_y_min), is.null(params$variance_y_max)))
  stop("Set both variance_y_min and variance_y_max, or leave both null.")
if (!is.null(params$variance_y_min)) stopifnot(is_scalar(params$variance_y_min),
  is_scalar(params$variance_y_max), params$variance_y_max > params$variance_y_min)

if (!is.null(params$type1_y_max)) stopifnot(is_scalar(params$type1_y_max),
  params$type1_y_max > params$alpha, params$type1_y_max <= 1)

# Relative paths are resolved from the Rmd directory. Interactive chunks fall
# back to the working directory when knitr has no current input.
rmd_input <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
report_dir <- if (length(rmd_input) == 1L && !is.na(rmd_input) &&
  nzchar(rmd_input) && file.exists(rmd_input)) dirname(normalizePath(rmd_input)) else getwd()
#' Resolve report input and output paths
#'
#' Expand a home-directory prefix and anchor relative paths to report_dir.
#'
#' @param path Nonempty character scalar path, relative or absolute.
#' @return Character resolved path; invalid path strings cause an error.
#' @details Uses report_dir from setup. It does not require the target to exist or
#'   normalize away relative path components.
resolve_path <- function(path) {
  if (!is.character(path) || length(path) != 1L || is.na(path) || !nzchar(path))
    stop("Input and output paths must be nonempty strings.")
  path <- path.expand(path)
  absolute <- grepl("^(/|[A-Za-z]:[/\\\\]|\\\\\\\\)", path)
  if (absolute) path else file.path(report_dir, path)
}
input_path <- resolve_path(params$results_dir)
output_path <- resolve_path(params$output_dir)
dir.create(output_path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!dir.exists(output_path)) stop("Cannot create output directory: ", output_path)
output_path <- normalizePath(output_path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
#' Export a report table as CSV
#'
#' Write one analysis or audit table into the configured output directory.
#'
#' @param x Data frame or table object accepted by write.csv().
#' @param filename Character file name within output_path.
#' @return NULL invisibly; creates or replaces the named CSV file.
#' @details Uses output_path from setup; omits row names and writes missing entries as
#'   NA.
write_table <- function(x, filename) utils::write.csv(x, file.path(output_path, filename),
  row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
method_levels <- c("Proposed-t-test", "Proposed-lm")
method_labels <- c("Two-sample t-test", "Linear working model")
normal_mc_quantile <- stats::qnorm((1 + params$mc_conf_level) / 2)
critical_value <- stats::qnorm(1 - params$alpha / 2)
```

## Input and interpretation

Place this Rmd in the **same directory** as `seed1.RData`, `seed2.RData`, and so on,
and click **Knit**. No simulation source file or helper script is required for this
report. It only reads saved outputs: it does **not** regenerate observations,
treatment assignments, or bootstrap samples.

This report is matched to
`simu_variance_one_seed_2100_s2_conditionalX2_gexp_order3_knot0.R`.
Its Scenario (ii) has $X\sim N(0,1)$ conditional on $-2<X<2$ and
$g(X)=e^X$. Its balancing splines have order three (degree two), one fixed
interior knot at zero for every sample size, and boundary knots $-2$ and $2$.
Scenarios (i) and (iii) are also included, with their settings unchanged by this
report.
There is **no one/two/three-knot schedule check** in this report.
Recorded metadata are checked against the conditional-normal, fixed-zero-knot
settings; this does not retrospectively verify how the observations were generated.

The main figure contains treatment-effect **variance ratios in the upper row**
and **Type I error in the lower row**, with one column per selected scenario.
The combined figure uses grey scenario strips, coral circles/solid lines for the
two-sample $t$-test, teal triangles/dashed lines for the linear working model,
transparent bands, and a single legend below both rows, as in the example.
Only the full treatment-effect variances are plotted, not the separate bootstrap
imbalance components. The shaded regions connect pointwise Monte Carlo confidence
intervals at the observed sample sizes; they are not simultaneous confidence bands.

For the CSV output of the same simulation script, change `file_pattern` to
`"^variance_seed_[0-9]+[.]csv$"`. Alternatively, `results_dir` may point to one combined
`.RData`, `.rds`, or `.csv` file. Do not load both RData and CSV copies of the same
repetitions. Keep different simulation designs in separate directories.

**This file expects the data-frame outputs of the attached variance-study script.**
It does not accept the rejection-indicator vectors returned by the separate
`simu_ball_corrected_s2_conditionalX2_gexp.R` or
`simu_updated_empirical_bootstrap_s2_conditionalX2_gexp.R` scripts.

## Read and validate results

```{r read-results}
#' Recognize a variance-study data frame
#'
#' Check for the core repetition, scenario, trial-size, and method columns.
#'
#' @param x Object to inspect.
#' @return Scalar logical indicating whether x is a data frame with replicate, scenario,
#'   n, and method columns.
#' @details This checks shape and column names only; numeric values and settings are
#'   validated later.
looks_like_results <- function(x) is.data.frame(x) &&
  all(c("replicate", "scenario", "n", "method") %in% names(x))
#' Read one saved variance-study result file
#'
#' Load compatible RData/rda, RDS, or CSV results without regenerating any simulation
#' data.
#'
#' @param path Character scalar path to a saved result file.
#' @return Compatible result data frame, preserving its saved rows and columns;
#'   unsupported or ambiguous inputs cause an error.
#' @details For RData files, loads into a private environment, prefers a compatible
#'   object res1, and otherwise requires exactly one compatible data frame. Rejection-
#'   indicator vectors are rejected.
read_one <- function(path) {
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(path))
  if (ext %in% c("rdata", "rda")) {
    env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    objects <- load(path, envir = env)
    # Candidate callback: nm is a loaded object name; returns TRUE for a compatible result
    # data frame.
    candidates <- objects[vapply(objects, function(nm) looks_like_results(env[[nm]]), logical(1))]
    if ("res1" %in% candidates) x <- env[["res1"]] else {
      if (length(candidates) != 1L) stop("Expected res1 or one compatible data frame in ", path,
        ". A numeric rejection vector is not a variance-study result.")
      x <- env[[candidates]]
    }
  } else if (ext == "rds") x <- readRDS(path) else if (ext == "csv") {
    x <- utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  } else stop("Unsupported input extension in ", path)
  if (!looks_like_results(x)) stop("Not a variance-study data frame: ", path)
  x
}
#' Convert a result column to numeric without hiding conversion failures
#'
#' Convert factor labels or saved values and check whether nonmissing inputs became NA.
#'
#' @param x Column vector to convert.
#' @param name Column name used in error messages.
#' @param path Input file or diagnostic label used in errors.
#' @return Numeric vector of the same length, retaining pre-existing missing values;
#'   invalid conversions cause an error.
#' @details Finiteness is checked separately at the relevant analysis stage.
as_num <- function(x, name, path) {
  if (is.factor(x)) x <- as.character(x)
  out <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  if (any(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))) stop("Non-numeric ", name, " in ", path)
  out
}
#' Read a numeric column through compatible saved aliases
#'
#' Select a supported column name and verify that multiple aliases agree.
#'
#' @param x Input result data frame.
#' @param aliases Character vector of accepted column names in preference order.
#' @param path Input path or diagnostic label used in errors.
#' @param required Logical flag; default TRUE requires at least one alias.
#' @return Numeric column vector; if optional and absent, a length-nrow(x) vector of
#'   NA_real_. Missing required columns or inconsistent aliases cause an error.
#' @details Uses as_num() and an all.equal() tolerance of 1e-10 for multiple present
#'   aliases.
pick_num <- function(x, aliases, path, required = TRUE) {
  present <- aliases[aliases %in% names(x)]
  if (!length(present)) {
    if (required) stop("Missing ", paste(aliases, collapse = " / "), " in ", path)
    return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(x)))
  }
  # Alias callback: nm is one present column name; returns its validated numeric column.
  values <- lapply(present, function(nm) as_num(x[[nm]], nm, path))
  if (length(values) > 1L) for (j in 2:length(values)) {
    if (!isTRUE(all.equal(values[[1]], values[[j]], tolerance = 1e-10,
                         check.attributes = FALSE)))
      stop("Alias columns disagree: ", paste(present, collapse = ", "), " in ", path)
  }
  values[[1]]
}
metadata_names <- c("study", "code_id", "B", "base_seed", "backend", "quadrature", "edge_grid",
  "R_version", "mgcv_version", "MASS_version", "splines2_version", "Rcpp_version",
  "outer_seed", "bootstrap_seed", "reference_seed", "scenario2_interior_knots",
  "scenario2_knot_location", "scenario2_knot_rule", "scenario2_X_transform",
  "scenario2_X_lower", "scenario2_X_upper", "scenario2_g_function",
  "scenario2_spline_order", "scenario2_spline_degree", "scenario2_feature_dimension")
#' Normalize saved result columns and verify variance scaling
#'
#' Construct a common result layout, retain metadata, and check aliases plus the 4/n
#' component decomposition.
#'
#' @param x Compatible data frame read from one input file.
#' @param path Source file path used for diagnostics and provenance.
#' @return Data frame containing identifiers, effect, three treatment estimate/variance
#'   columns, status/error/warnings, source_file, metadata, and optional
#'   base/sigma_E/sigma_m/adjusted_sigma2 columns.
#' @details Uses metadata_names from the surrounding chunk. Where finite components are
#'   available, checks treatment_variance = 4*adjusted_sigma2/n =
#'   4*(base+sigma_E+sigma_m)/n. Missing optional columns remain NA and are not inferred.
standardize <- function(x, path) {
  if (!"effect" %in% names(x)) stop("Missing effect in ", path, "; cannot verify null simulations.")
  out <- data.frame(replicate = as_num(x$replicate, "replicate", path),
    scenario = as.character(x$scenario), n = as_num(x$n, "n", path),
    method = as.character(x$method), effect = as_num(x$effect, "effect", path),
    treatment_estimate = pick_num(x, c("treatment_estimate", "estimate"), path),
    treatment_variance = pick_num(x, c("treatment_variance", "variance"), path),
    mc_treatment_estimate = pick_num(x, c("mc_treatment_estimate", "mc_estimate"), path),
    status = if ("status" %in% names(x)) as.character(x$status) else "ok",
    error = if ("error" %in% names(x)) as.character(x$error) else "",
    warnings = if ("warnings" %in% names(x)) as.character(x$warnings) else "",
    source_file = path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (nm in metadata_names) out[[nm]] <- if (nm %in% names(x))
    as.character(x[[nm]]) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(x))
  for (nm in c("base", "sigma_E", "sigma_m", "adjusted_sigma2"))
    out[[nm]] <- pick_num(x, nm, path, required = FALSE)
  expected <- 4 / out$n * out$adjusted_sigma2
  ok <- is.finite(expected) & is.finite(out$treatment_variance)
  if (any(abs(expected[ok] - out$treatment_variance[ok]) >
      1e-9 * pmax(1, abs(expected[ok]), abs(out$treatment_variance[ok]))))
    stop("The 4/n variance-scale check failed in ", path)
  from_components <- 4 / out$n * (out$base + out$sigma_E + out$sigma_m)
  ok <- is.finite(from_components) & is.finite(out$treatment_variance)
  if (any(abs(from_components[ok] - out$treatment_variance[ok]) >
      1e-9 * pmax(1, abs(from_components[ok]), abs(out$treatment_variance[ok]))))
    stop("Saved full variance does not match base + sigma_E + sigma_m in ", path)
  out
}
if (dir.exists(input_path)) {
  input_files <- list.files(input_path, pattern = params$file_pattern,
    full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE)
  input_files <- input_files[!dir.exists(input_files)]
} else if (file.exists(input_path)) input_files <- input_path else stop("Input not found: ", input_path)
if (!length(input_files)) stop("No seed files matched in ", input_path,
  ". Place this Rmd beside the saved seed*.RData files, not just beside the R source. ",
  "This report does not run delta() or generate new simulation datasets.")
input_files <- sort(normalizePath(input_files, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE))
write_table(data.frame(path = input_files, bytes = file.info(input_files)$size), "input_manifest.csv")
# Input callback: p is one file path; returns its standardized data frame before stacking
# rows.
results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(input_files, function(p) standardize(read_one(p), p)))
rownames(results) <- NULL
if (anyNA(results$scenario) || anyNA(results$method) ||
    any(!results$scenario %in% scenario_levels) || any(!results$method %in% method_levels))
  stop("Unexpected scenario/method labels. Expected i/ii/iii and Proposed-t-test/Proposed-lm.")
if (any(!is.finite(results$n) | results$n < 1 | results$n != floor(results$n)) ||
    any(!is.finite(results$replicate) | results$replicate < 1 |
        results$replicate != floor(results$replicate))) stop("Invalid n or repetition identifier.")
results <- results[results$scenario %in% selected_scenarios &
  results$n >= params$n_min & results$n <= params$n_max, , drop = FALSE]
if (!nrow(results)) stop("No rows remain for the selected scenarios/sample-size range.")
key <- paste(results$replicate, results$scenario, results$n, results$method, sep = "|")
dup <- duplicated(key) | duplicated(key, fromLast = TRUE)
if (any(dup)) {
  write_table(results[dup, , drop = FALSE], "duplicate_rows.csv")
  stop("Duplicate repetition/scenario/n/method rows; inspect duplicate_rows.csv.")
}
if (any(!is.finite(results$effect)) ||
    any(abs(results$effect - params$null_value) > 1e-10 * max(1, abs(params$null_value))))
  stop("The saved true effects do not all equal null_value. Do not label power as Type I error.")

# Never pool different implementations, bootstrap sizes, seeds, or fitting versions.
for (nm in c("study", "code_id", "B", "base_seed", "backend", "quadrature", "edge_grid",
             "R_version", "mgcv_version", "MASS_version", "splines2_version", "Rcpp_version")) {
  nonempty <- !is.na(results[[nm]]) & nzchar(results[[nm]])
  if (any(nonempty) && !all(nonempty)) stop("Partly missing metadata: ", nm)
  vals <- unique(results[[nm]][nonempty])
  if (length(vals) > 1L) stop("Mixed ", nm, " values. Analyze each batch separately.")
}
expected_study <- "empirical_X_only_variance_v8_2100_s2_conditionalX2_gexp_order3_knot0"
if (isTRUE(params$check_scenario2_settings)) {
  supplied_study <- unique(results$study[!is.na(results$study)])
  if (length(supplied_study) && any(supplied_study != expected_study))
    stop("These files have a different study identifier. This report is for ", expected_study,
      ". Do not mix clipped-X, transformed-X, or increasing-knot runs.")
  ii <- results$scenario == "ii"
  if (any(ii)) {
    checks <- list(scenario2_interior_knots = 1, scenario2_knot_location = 0,
      scenario2_X_lower = -2, scenario2_X_upper = 2,
      scenario2_spline_order = 3, scenario2_spline_degree = 2,
      scenario2_feature_dimension = 4)
    missing_checks <- character()
    for (nm in names(checks)) {
      raw <- results[[nm]][ii]
      if (all(is.na(raw))) { missing_checks <- c(missing_checks, nm); next }
      value <- as_num(raw, nm, "Scenario (ii) metadata")
      if (any(!is.finite(value)) || any(abs(value - checks[[nm]]) > 1e-10))
        stop("Scenario (ii) metadata mismatch: ", nm, " must be ", checks[[nm]], ".")
    }
    text_checks <- c(scenario2_X_transform = "conditional_normal[-2,2]",
      scenario2_knot_rule = "fixed_zero", scenario2_g_function = "exp(X)")
    for (nm in names(text_checks)) {
      value <- results[[nm]][ii]
      target <- unname(text_checks[nm])
      if (all(is.na(value))) missing_checks <- c(missing_checks, nm) else
        if (anyNA(value) || any(value != target)) stop("Scenario (ii) metadata mismatch: ", nm,
          "; expected ", target, ".")
    }
    if (length(missing_checks)) warning("Could not verify missing Scenario (ii) metadata: ",
      paste(missing_checks, collapse = ", "), ". No values were inferred.")
  }
}
write_table(unique(results[, c("scenario", "n", metadata_names[grepl("^scenario2_", metadata_names)])]),
  "scenario2_settings.csv")

# Check seed overlap across experiments, allowing the two methods to share a trial.
seed_records <- unique(results[, c("replicate", "scenario", "n", "outer_seed", "reference_seed")])
outer_seeds <- seed_records$outer_seed[!is.na(seed_records$outer_seed)]
reference_seeds <- seed_records$reference_seed[!is.na(seed_records$reference_seed)]
if (anyDuplicated(outer_seeds) || anyDuplicated(reference_seeds) ||
    length(intersect(outer_seeds, reference_seeds)))
  stop("Repeated or overlapping original/reference trial seeds detected; cannot assume independent references.")

status_ok <- !is.na(results$status) & results$status == "ok"
results$variance_evaluable <- status_ok & is.finite(results$treatment_variance)
results$reference_evaluable <- status_ok & is.finite(results$mc_treatment_estimate)
results$estimate_evaluable <- status_ok & is.finite(results$treatment_estimate)
# A finite positive saved contrast variance is required to define the normal test.
results$test_evaluable <- results$estimate_evaluable & results$variance_evaluable &
  results$treatment_variance > 0
results$test_statistic <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(results))
results$reject <- rep(NA, nrow(results))
ok <- results$test_evaluable
results$test_statistic[ok] <- (results$treatment_estimate[ok] - params$null_value) /
  sqrt(results$treatment_variance[ok])
results$reject[ok] <- abs(results$test_statistic[ok]) > critical_value
invalid <- !results$test_evaluable | !results$reference_evaluable
write_table(results[invalid, c("replicate", "scenario", "n", "method", "status", "error", "warnings",
  "treatment_estimate", "treatment_variance", "mc_treatment_estimate", "source_file")], "invalid_rows.csv")
if (any(invalid)) {
  msg <- paste(sum(invalid), "rows contain failed/undefined tests or references; see invalid_rows.csv.")
  if (params$invalid_policy == "stop") stop(msg) else warning(msg,
    " Rates are conditional on evaluable tests where necessary; no variance is clipped or repaired.")
}
cat("Loaded", length(input_files), "file(s),", nrow(results), "rows, and",
    length(unique(results$replicate)), "distinct repetition identifiers.\n")
```

## Variance and Type I error calculations

The variance plot displays
\[
R_{a,n}=\frac{\operatorname{mean}(\widehat V_{\tau,a,n})}
{\operatorname{var}(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{MC}}_{a,n})}.
\]
` treatment_variance ` (or its alias `variance`) is already on the treatment-effect
scale, $\widehat V_{\tau,a,n}=4\widehat\sigma_{a,\mathrm{adj}}^2/n$.
**No extra factor of $4/n$ is applied.** The denominator is the sample variance of
independent reference treatment-effect estimates, not the variance of the
estimated variances.

For positive $\overline V$ and $V_M$, the pointwise ratio interval is
\[
\frac{\overline V}{V_M}\exp\left\{\pm z_{(1+c)/2}
\sqrt{(s_B/\overline V)^2+(s_M/V_M)^2}\right\},
\]
where $c$ is `mc_conf_level`, $s_B$ is the standard error of the mean estimated
variance, and $s_M$ is the fourth-moment plug-in standard error of the reference
sample variance, using the formula in the supplied simulation script.
The original and reference sets are treated as independent, as constructed by
the source. These are approximate Monte Carlo intervals, not exact intervals.

For Type I error, this report explicitly applies a **two-sided normal-reference
test** to the saved outputs:
\[
\left|\frac{\widehat\tau-\tau_0}{\sqrt{\widehat V_\tau}}\right|
>\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
Each dataset uses its own feasible adjusted variance, not the Monte Carlo
reference variance or an oracle variance. The default $\tau_0$ is zero and
$\alpha=0.05$. The source saves estimates and variances, not rejection indicators;
this testing rule is the analysis performed here. Binomial intervals are computed
with `stats::binom.test()`.

```{r summaries}
#' Calculate a mean when observations are available
#'
#' Provide a scalar fallback for empty diagnostic subsets.
#'
#' @param x Numeric vector, already filtered to the observations to summarize.
#' @return mean(x), or NA_real_ when x is empty.
#' @details Does not remove missing values.
mean_or_na <- function(x) if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_
#' Calculate a sample standard deviation when defined
#'
#' Provide a scalar fallback for subsets with fewer than two observations.
#'
#' @param x Numeric vector, already filtered to the observations to summarize.
#' @return Sample standard deviation, or NA_real_ when length(x) < 2.
#' @details Does not remove missing values.
sd_or_na <- function(x) if (length(x) >= 2L) stats::sd(x) else NA_real_
#' Calculate empirical quantiles with an empty-subset fallback
#'
#' Return unnamed quantiles for selected studentized-test diagnostics.
#'
#' @param x Numeric vector of selected observations.
#' @param p Quantile probability or probabilities supplied to quantile().
#' @return Unnamed numeric quantile vector, or scalar NA_real_ for an empty x.
#' @details Uses the default quantile definition and does not remove missing values.
q_or_na <- function(x, p) if (length(x)) unname(stats::quantile(x, p)) else NA_real_
#' Estimate Monte Carlo uncertainty in the reference sample variance
#'
#' Apply the same fourth-moment plug-in calculation as vc_variance_se() in the simulation
#' source.
#'
#' @param x Numeric vector of independent, finite reference treatment contrasts.
#' @return Scalar standard error of var(x), or NA_real_ when fewer than four observations
#'   are present.
#' @details The fourth central moment estimates variance-of-variance uncertainty. This
#'   quantity differs from sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)), which is the SE of a mean.
variance_mcse <- function(x) {
  # Matches vc_variance_se() in the supplied R source.
  m <- length(x)
  if (m < 4L) return(NA_real_)
  v <- stats::var(x)
  fourth <- mean((x - mean(x))^4)
  sqrt(max(0, (fourth - (m - 3) / (m - 1) * v^2) / m))
}
sample_sizes <- sort(unique(results$n))
grid <- expand.grid(scenario = selected_scenarios, n = sample_sizes,
  method = method_levels, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
vs <- ts <- ds <- vector("list", nrow(grid))
for (j in seq_len(nrow(grid))) {
  cell <- grid[j, , drop = FALSE]
  z <- results[results$scenario == cell$scenario & results$n == cell$n &
               results$method == cell$method, , drop = FALSE]
  v <- z$treatment_variance[z$variance_evaluable]
  ref <- z$mc_treatment_estimate[z$reference_evaluable]
  estimates <- z$treatment_estimate[z$estimate_evaluable]
  R <- length(v); M <- length(ref)
  # se_b is the SE of the mean variance estimate: sd(v)/sqrt(R), not sd(v) alone.
  mv <- mean_or_na(v); se_b <- sd_or_na(v) / sqrt(R)
  rv <- if (M >= 2L) stats::var(ref) else NA_real_
  se_m <- variance_mcse(ref)
  ratio <- lo <- hi <- log_se <- NA_real_
  reason <- "Not enough original/reference results for a variance ratio"
  if (R >= 1L && is.finite(rv) && rv > 0) {
    ratio <- mv / rv
    reason <- "Point estimate only; need >=2 original and >=4 reference results for an interval"
    if (R >= 2L && M >= 4L && is.finite(se_b) && is.finite(se_m)) {
      if (mv > 0) {
        # Independent numerator/denominator contributions add on the log-ratio scale.
        # Dividing each SE by its mean/variance converts it to relative uncertainty.
        log_se <- sqrt((se_b / mv)^2 + (se_m / rv)^2)
        lo <- exp(log(ratio) - normal_mc_quantile * log_se)
        hi <- exp(log(ratio) + normal_mc_quantile * log_se)
        reason <- "Log delta method; independent original/reference samples"
      } else {
        # A log interval is unavailable for a nonpositive numerator; use the linear delta
        # formula.
        ratio_se <- sqrt((se_b / rv)^2 + (mv * se_m / rv^2)^2)
        lo <- ratio - normal_mc_quantile * ratio_se
        hi <- ratio + normal_mc_quantile * ratio_se
        reason <- "Linear delta method because mean estimated variance is nonpositive"
      }
    }
  } else if (is.finite(rv) && rv == 0) reason <- "Zero reference treatment-effect variance; ratio undefined"
  if (!is.finite(lo) || !is.finite(hi)) {
    lo <- hi <- NA_real_
    if (is.finite(ratio) && R >= 2L && M >= 4L) reason <- "Interval overflow/nonfinite; see original/reference summaries"
  }
  vs[[j]] <- data.frame(cell, datasets_loaded = nrow(z), outer_repetitions = R,
    mc_repetitions = M, mean_estimated_variance = mv, mean_estimate_mcse = se_b,
    reference_variance = rv, reference_mcse = se_m, variance_ratio = ratio,
    ratio_lower = lo, ratio_upper = hi, log_ratio_mcse = log_se, interval_status = reason,
    nonpositive_variances = sum(v <= 0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # Undefined tests are excluded from the rate denominator and reported as invalid.
  evaluable <- sum(z$test_evaluable); rejected <- sum(z$reject[z$test_evaluable])
  invalid_tests <- nrow(z) - evaluable
  rate <- if (evaluable) rejected / evaluable else NA_real_
  ci <- if (evaluable) as.numeric(stats::binom.test(rejected, evaluable,
    conf.level = params$mc_conf_level)$conf.int) else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
  # Binomial limits quantify MC uncertainty; all-loaded bounds instead allow either
  # outcome for invalid tests.
  ts[[j]] <- data.frame(cell, datasets_loaded = nrow(z), evaluable_tests = evaluable,
    invalid_tests = invalid_tests, rejections = rejected, type1_error = rate,
    lower = ci[1], upper = ci[2], alpha = params$alpha, null_value = params$null_value,
    critical_value = critical_value,
    all_loaded_rate_lower = if (nrow(z)) rejected / nrow(z) else NA_real_,
    all_loaded_rate_upper = if (nrow(z)) (rejected + invalid_tests) / nrow(z) else NA_real_,
    rate_interpretation = if (!nrow(z)) "No saved datasets" else if (invalid_tests)
      "Conditional on an evaluable test" else "All loaded null datasets", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  student <- z$test_statistic[z$test_evaluable]
  errs <- estimates - params$null_value
  # Diagnostic rows retain bias, studentization, failures, and a reference-scaled
  # rejection check.
  ds[[j]] <- data.frame(cell, datasets_loaded = nrow(z),
    failed_status = sum(is.na(z$status) | z$status != "ok"),
    finite_variance_estimates = R, finite_reference_estimates = M,
    evaluable_tests = evaluable, nonpositive_variances = sum(v <= 0),
    rows_with_warnings = sum(!is.na(z$warnings) & nzchar(z$warnings)),
    estimate_bias = mean_or_na(errs), bias_mcse = sd_or_na(errs) / sqrt(length(errs)),
    studentized_mean = mean_or_na(student), studentized_sd = sd_or_na(student),
    studentized_q025 = q_or_na(student, 0.025), studentized_q975 = q_or_na(student, 0.975),
    left_rejection_rate = if (length(student)) mean(student < -critical_value) else NA_real_,
    right_rejection_rate = if (length(student)) mean(student > critical_value) else NA_real_,
    reference_scaled_rejection_diagnostic = if (length(errs) && is.finite(rv) && rv > 0)
      mean(abs(errs / sqrt(rv)) > critical_value) else NA_real_)
}
variance_summary <- do.call(rbind, vs)
type1_summary <- do.call(rbind, ts)
diagnostics <- do.call(rbind, ds)
#' Sort numerical summary rows consistently
#'
#' Order scenario, sample size, and working model for CSV tables and diagnostics.
#'
#' @param x Data frame containing scenario, n, and method.
#' @return Data frame with the same columns and rows in the requested order.
#' @details Uses scenario_levels and method_levels from setup; row names are retained.
order_rows <- function(x) x[order(match(x$scenario, scenario_levels), x$n,
  match(x$method, method_levels)), , drop = FALSE]
variance_summary <- order_rows(variance_summary)
type1_summary <- order_rows(type1_summary)
diagnostics <- order_rows(diagnostics)
write_table(variance_summary, "treatment_effect_variance_ratio_summary.csv")
write_table(type1_summary, "type1_error_summary.csv")
write_table(diagnostics, "simulation_diagnostics.csv")
write_table(diagnostics[diagnostics$scenario == "ii", ], "scenario_ii_diagnostics.csv")
if (any(diagnostics$datasets_loaded == 0L)) warning("Some scenario/n/method cells are missing; they are not filled in.")
if (any(!is.finite(variance_summary$ratio_lower))) warning(
  "Some ratio intervals are unavailable. Points/intervals are drawn only when defined; see interval_status in the CSV.")
if (any(diagnostics$datasets_loaded > 0 & diagnostics$datasets_loaded < 100L)) warning(
  "Some cells have fewer than 100 saved repetitions. Type I error and variance comparisons may be very imprecise.")
knitr::kable(diagnostics[, c("scenario", "n", "method", "datasets_loaded", "failed_status",
  "finite_variance_estimates", "finite_reference_estimates", "evaluable_tests", "nonpositive_variances")],
  caption = "Loaded and evaluable dataset counts")
```

A single `delta(i)` output contains one original and one independent reference
trial per scenario/sample-size cell, analyzed with both working models. It is
not enough to calculate a reference sampling variance. With too few repetitions,
the report displays the available quantities and lists unavailable intervals,
rather than fabricating a reference variance or aborting with an unexplained error.
For Monte Carlo precision, compare the reported counts with your planned number
of repetitions; completely absent seed files cannot be diagnosed from the files
that are present.

With `invalid_policy: "report"`, finite nonpositive estimates remain in the
variance comparison, but their tests are **undefined**, not counted as
non-rejections. Rates then condition on evaluable tests. Failures and warnings
are saved separately. The `all_loaded_rate_lower` and `all_loaded_rate_upper`
columns give logical bounds if undefined tests could have either outcome; they
are not confidence intervals. Set `invalid_policy: "stop"` to stop when an invalid
row is found. Source failures can also remove a reference estimate; summaries
from retained runs should not be treated as unconditional performance when this occurs.

## Variance ratios and Type I error

```{r plot, fig.cap="Full treatment-effect variance ratios (upper row) and empirical Type I error (lower row). Shading connects pointwise Monte Carlo intervals, not simultaneous confidence bands."}
#' Add ordered labels for figure facets and working models
#'
#' Prepare summary rows for the common ggplot scales and scenario layout.
#'
#' @param x Summary data frame containing scenario, method, and n.
#' @return Data frame with scenario_label and method_label factors added, sorted by those
#'   labels and n.
#' @details Uses selected_scenarios, method_levels, and method_labels from setup.
#'   Numerical estimates and intervals are unchanged.
label_data <- function(x) {
  x$scenario_label <- factor(x$scenario, levels = selected_scenarios,
    labels = paste0("Scenario (", selected_scenarios, ")"))
  x$method_label <- factor(x$method, levels = method_levels, labels = method_labels)
  x[order(x$scenario_label, x$method_label, x$n), , drop = FALSE]
}
variance_plot_data <- label_data(variance_summary)
type1_plot_data <- label_data(type1_summary)
write_table(variance_plot_data, "treatment_effect_variance_ratio_plot_data.csv")
write_table(type1_plot_data, "type1_error_plot_data.csv")

# Match the two colours and the circle/triangle + solid/dashed encoding
# in the supplied example. The same scales on both rows collect into one legend.
method_colours <- setNames(c("#F8766D", "#00BFC4"), method_labels)
plot_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 13) + theme(
  strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey85", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.6),
  strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, margin = margin(6, 0, 6, 0)),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(0.8, "lines"),
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 11),
  axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)),
  axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
  legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal", legend.box = "horizontal",
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13), legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
  legend.key.width = grid::unit(1, "cm"),
  plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8)
)
method_scales <- list(
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Working model", values = method_colours,
    limits = method_labels, drop = FALSE),
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Working model", values = method_colours,
    limits = method_labels, drop = FALSE),
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Working model", limits = method_labels,
    values = setNames(c(16, 17), method_labels), drop = FALSE),
  scale_linetype_manual(name = "Working model", limits = method_labels,
    values = setNames(c("solid", "dashed"), method_labels), drop = FALSE),
  guides(fill = "none")
)

# Coordinate zooming changes only the visible range: it never removes values
# before constructing the lines or intervals. Warn about anything out of range.
#' Report values beyond a chosen display range
#'
#' Identify finite points or interval endpoints that coordinate zooming will hide.
#'
#' @param values Numeric vector of plot values and/or band endpoints.
#' @param bounds Length-2 numeric vector of lower and upper visible limits.
#' @param name Character plot name included in the warning.
#' @return NULL invisibly; emits a warning if any finite values are outside the bounds.
#' @details Does not filter, clip, or modify the plotted data or CSV summaries.
warn_outside <- function(values, bounds, name) {
  outside <- is.finite(values) & (values < bounds[1] | values > bounds[2])
  if (any(outside)) warning(name, ": some points or band endpoints extend outside ",
    paste(bounds, collapse = " to "), ". Enlarge the YAML axis range to see them. ",
    "All numerical results remain unchanged in the CSV files.")
}
variance_bounds <- if (is.null(params$variance_y_min)) NULL else
  c(params$variance_y_min, params$variance_y_max)
finite_upper <- type1_summary$upper[is.finite(type1_summary$upper)]
type1_top <- if (is.null(params$type1_y_max))
  min(1, max(c(2 * params$alpha, finite_upper)) * 1.08) else params$type1_y_max
conditional_rates <- any(type1_summary$invalid_tests > 0)

# TOP ROW: full treatment-effect variance ratio, not the imbalance component.
g_variance <- ggplot(variance_plot_data,
  aes(n, variance_ratio, colour = method_label, shape = method_label,
      linetype = method_label, group = method_label)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = n, ymin = ratio_lower, ymax = ratio_upper,
    fill = method_label, group = method_label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    stat = "identity", position = "identity", alpha = params$band_alpha,
    colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.65) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85, na.rm = TRUE) + geom_point(size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ scenario_label, nrow = 1, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sample_sizes, limits = range(sample_sizes),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.04)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = if (is.null(variance_bounds)) waiver() else
    seq(variance_bounds[1], variance_bounds[2], by = 0.1),
    #' Format variance axis labels
    #'
    #' Convert numeric tick positions into figure label strings.
    #'
    #' @param x Numeric vector of axis tick values.
    #' @return Character vector of one-decimal labels.
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Treatment-effect variance ratio") + method_scales + plot_theme
if (!is.null(variance_bounds)) {
  g_variance <- g_variance + coord_cartesian(ylim = variance_bounds)
  warn_outside(unlist(variance_plot_data[c("variance_ratio", "ratio_lower", "ratio_upper")]),
    variance_bounds, "Variance display")
}

# BOTTOM ROW: two-sided normal-reference tests using each trial's saved variance.
g_type1 <- ggplot(type1_plot_data,
  aes(n, type1_error, colour = method_label, shape = method_label,
      linetype = method_label, group = method_label)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = n, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = method_label, group = method_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, stat = "identity", position = "identity",
    alpha = params$band_alpha, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = params$alpha, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.65) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85, na.rm = TRUE) + geom_point(size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ scenario_label, nrow = 1, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sample_sizes, limits = range(sample_sizes),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.04)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = if (type1_top <= 0.13) seq(0, type1_top, by = 0.03) else waiver(),
    #' Format percentage axis labels
    #'
    #' Convert numeric tick positions into figure label strings.
    #'
    #' @param x Numeric vector of axis tick values.
    #' @return Character vector of one-decimal percentages, after multiplying values by
    #'   100.
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, type1_top)) +
  labs(x = "Sample size", y = if (conditional_rates)
    "Rejection rate among evaluable tests" else "Empirical Type I error") +
  method_scales + plot_theme
warn_outside(unlist(type1_plot_data[c("type1_error", "lower", "upper")]),
  c(0, type1_top), "Type I error display")

# Object requested for interactive use: run this chunk, then enter g2.
g2 <- patchwork::wrap_plots(g_variance, g_type1, ncol = 1,
  heights = c(1, 1), guides = "collect")
g2 <- g2 & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
combined_plot <- g2  # Keep the earlier name as an alias.
print(g2)

#' Export a ggplot or combined patchwork figure
#'
#' Save the displayed figure as a high-resolution PNG and optionally PDF.
#'
#' @param p ggplot or patchwork plot object.
#' @param name Character output basename without an extension.
#' @param width Figure width in inches; default 12.
#' @param height Figure height in inches; default 9.
#' @return PDF filename invisibly when a PDF is saved, otherwise NULL invisibly. Always
#'   writes name.png and, when enabled, name.pdf.
#' @details Uses output_path and params$save_pdf. PNG output is 400 DPI with a white
#'   background; PDFs disable Dingbats fonts.
save_plot <- function(p, name, width = 12, height = 9) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_path, paste0(name, ".png")), plot = p,
    width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 400, bg = "white")
  if (isTRUE(params$save_pdf)) ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_path, paste0(name, ".pdf")),
    plot = p, width = width, height = height, units = "in",
    device = grDevices::pdf, useDingbats = FALSE, bg = "white")
}
save_plot(g2, "variance_ratio_type1_conditionalX2_gexp")
save_plot(g_variance, "treatment_effect_variance_ratio_bands", height = 4.2)
save_plot(g_type1, "type1_error_bands", height = 4.6)
if (isTRUE(params$save_plot_object)) saveRDS(g2, file.path(output_path, "g2.rds"))
```


The horizontal reference is **one** for the variance ratio and
**`r sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * params$alpha)`** for Type I error. Standard-normal
critical values are used for both working-model estimators in this report.
The confidence level is **`r sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * params$mc_conf_level)`**.

The default variance axis is **0.7 to 1.2**, and the Type I error axis is
**0 to 11.5%**, matching the example. Change `variance_y_min: 0.6` for a wider
variance display. Set both variance limits to `null`, or `type1_y_max: null`,
for automatic ranges. Coordinate zooming does not change estimates or intervals;
a warning identifies any hidden endpoints. `band_alpha` controls transparency.
To show only one scenario, use, for example, `scenarios: ["iii"]`.

### Display the figure as `g2` in the console

Running this Rmd's chunks interactively creates `g2` in the current R session.
Knitting in RStudio normally uses a separate session, so knitting alone need not
create a console object. The report also saves `g2.rds`. After knitting, run:

```{r display-g2-later, eval=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
g2 <- readRDS("variance_type1_conditionalX2_gexp_plots/g2.rds")
g2
```

These paths assume the console working directory is the folder containing the
Rmd. Loading `g2.rds` neither reads the seed files again nor reruns the simulation.

## Numerical summaries

```{r numerical-tables}
knitr::kable(variance_summary[, c("scenario", "n", "method", "outer_repetitions", "mc_repetitions",
  "mean_estimated_variance", "reference_variance", "variance_ratio", "ratio_lower", "ratio_upper")],
  digits = 5, caption = "Full treatment-effect variance: estimated mean, reference variance, and ratio")
knitr::kable(type1_summary[, c("scenario", "n", "method", "evaluable_tests", "invalid_tests",
  "rejections", "type1_error", "lower", "upper")], digits = 4,
  caption = "Rejection rates and pointwise binomial intervals")
knitr::kable(diagnostics[, c("scenario", "n", "method", "estimate_bias", "bias_mcse",
  "studentized_mean", "studentized_sd", "left_rejection_rate", "right_rejection_rate")],
  digits = 4, caption = "Additional studentized-test diagnostics")
```

These diagnostics do not identify a cause of miscalibration by themselves.
Agreement of an average variance with a sampling variance does not guarantee
calibration of dataset-specific studentized statistics. The CSV also records
`reference_scaled_rejection_diagnostic`, using a common independent reference
standard deviation instead of estimated dataset-specific denominators. This is
an **infeasible diagnostic**, not a replacement test; its reference standard
deviation is itself estimated.

## Saved files and reproducibility

The output directory is **`r output_path`**. It contains the combined figure,
separate row figures, ratio and rejection-rate CSV summaries, pointwise plot data,
input/settings records, and failure/calibration diagnostics. Input data files
are never overwritten.

```{r record-settings}
settings <- data.frame(setting = c("results_dir", "output_dir", "scenarios", "n_min", "n_max",
  "alpha", "null_value", "mc_conf_level", "band_alpha", "invalid_policy", "check_scenario2_settings",
  "test_rule", "variance_scale", "ratio_interval", "variance_y_min", "variance_y_max",
  "type1_y_max", "expected_study"),
  value = c(input_path, output_path, paste(selected_scenarios, collapse = ","),
    as.character(params$n_min), as.character(params$n_max), as.character(params$alpha),
    as.character(params$null_value), as.character(params$mc_conf_level), as.character(params$band_alpha),
    params$invalid_policy, as.character(params$check_scenario2_settings),
    "Two-sided normal test using each dataset's saved treatment_variance",
    "Raw treatment-effect variance already includes 4/n; ratio cancels common scaling",
    "Log delta method with independent numerator/denominator uncertainty",
    if (is.null(params$variance_y_min)) "automatic" else as.character(params$variance_y_min),
    if (is.null(params$variance_y_max)) "automatic" else as.character(params$variance_y_max),
    if (is.null(params$type1_y_max)) "automatic" else as.character(params$type1_y_max),
    expected_study))
write_table(settings, "analysis_settings.csv")
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(output_path, "sessionInfo.txt"))
```

### Source and calculation notes

Input structure, variance scaling, settings, and the fourth-moment reference
variance standard error follow the attached
`simu_variance_one_seed_2100_s2_conditionalX2_gexp_order3_knot0.R`, specifically
`vc_outer_one()`, `vc_variance_se()`, `vc_metadata()`, `delta()`, and `vc_write_rdata()`.
The report adds the explicitly specified normal-reference tests and Monte Carlo
interval calculations. It does not modify any estimator or simulation scenario.

Software documentation: [binom.test](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/binom.test.html),
[geom_ribbon](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_ribbon.html), and
[patchwork::wrap_plots](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com/reference/wrap_plots.html).
